tradeoffs.loses: the seed=0 reproducibility hint on Router-bound requests (OpenAI's seed is best-effort and only within one model snapshot; the provider-fallback path still sends it)
tradeoffs.why: Every gpt/o1/o3 request in get_response_from_llm sends seed=0, which the runtime treats as untranslatable, so the whole OpenAI path stayed on the provider.

tradeoffs.loses: the pinned gpt-4o-2024-05-13 snapshot: Router serves catalog id gpt-4o (Router reports gpt-4o-2024-08-06), so review wording and scores move, and the ICLR-benchmark numbers in review_iclr_bench were measured on the 2024-05-13 snapshot
tradeoffs.why: The reviewer is the one stage whose model is hard-coded, and it is a dated id Router returns 404 for, so the whole review stage stayed on OpenAI.

tradeoffs.loses: gpt-4o's exact review behaviour: a different model generation writes the reviews, so scores and wording change and are no longer comparable with the paper's ICLR-benchmark numbers; it is also a reasoning model, so part of the fixed 4096-token output cap goes to reasoning
tradeoffs.why: The review stage is the app's most prompt-heavy stage and nobody is waiting on it: a background-grade Flex model is the natural fit.

tradeoffs.loses: Claude 3.5 Sonnet itself (Router's catalog starts at Claude 4.5): the default model becomes Claude Sonnet 5, so ideas, write-ups and reviews read differently; and the Claude branch stops sending temperature at all, so sampling is the model default instead of 0.75
tradeoffs.why: claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 is the app's default --model and is not in Router's catalog, so the default run routes nothing.
